# winpipe

[winpipe](https://github.com/jslth/winpipe) exposes Win32 Named Pipes as
R connections to read from and write to. Named Pipes are a device for
inter-process communication (IPC) that are part of the file system and
allow for fine-grained access control. R has native support for FIFOs on
Unix-like systems but does not expose any API for named pipes on
Windows.

Features:

- Create and serve Windows named pipes, i.e., R can be both client and
  server
- Named pipes are represented as native R connections, i.e., I/O works
  out of the box
- Let R talk to non-R processes
- Can accept clients without blocking the R session
- Includes an interface to
  [SDDL](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/secauthz/security-descriptor-definition-language)

## Installation

You can install the development version of winpipe from
[GitHub](https://github.com/) with:

``` r

# install.packages("pak")
pak::pak("jslth/winpipe")
```

## Example

To communicate between processes, a server and a client are required:

``` r

library(winpipe)

server <- winpipe("a-pipe")
client <- winpipe("a-pipe", server = FALSE)
```

Since winpipes are R connections, most I/O functions work out of the
box. You can, for example, pass the client as a file name to
[`write.csv()`](https://rdrr.io/r/utils/write.table.html):

``` r

write.csv(iris, file = client)
```

The server can then receive the data. Depending on the permissions, this
works in both directions (client → server and server → client)

``` r

head(read.csv(server))
#>   X Sepal.Length Sepal.Width Petal.Length Petal.Width Species
#> 1 1          5.1         3.5          1.4         0.2  setosa
#> 2 2          4.9         3.0          1.4         0.2  setosa
#> 3 3          4.7         3.2          1.3         0.2  setosa
#> 4 4          4.6         3.1          1.5         0.2  setosa
#> 5 5          5.0         3.6          1.4         0.2  setosa
#> 6 6          5.4         3.9          1.7         0.4  setosa
```

Beware, however, that reading consumes a payload. Another call to
[`read.csv()`](https://rdrr.io/r/utils/read.table.html) would result in
an error. You can peek a payload without consuming it using
[`np_peek()`](https://jslth.github.io/winpipe/reference/info.md). This
confirms that the payload has been consumed by giving the number of
bytes left to read.

``` r

np_peek(server)
#> [1] 0
```

One cool thing about named pipes is their access control. Named pipes
support security descriptors using
[DACL](https://de.wikipedia.org/wiki/Discretionary_Access_Control) and
[winpipe](https://github.com/jslth/winpipe) includes a small API to
construct ACLs. To allow only admins and the local system to access a
named pipe, you can do:

``` r

sd <- sd_create(
  ace(type = "deny", rights = "generic all", account = "everyone"),
  ace(type = "allow", rights = "generic all", account = "admins"),
  ace(type = "allow", rights = "generic all", account = "local system")
)
sd
#> <winpipe_sd>
#> D:(D;;GA;;;WD)(A;;GA;;;BA)(A;;GA;;;SY)
```

A winpipe created with this security descriptor will deny access to all
non-privileged users. You can pass this security descriptor to a pipe
you create and it will adhere to this access control.
[`np_sd()`](https://jslth.github.io/winpipe/reference/info.md) allows
you to read the security descriptor of a given named pipe (note that
Windows “normalizes” the descriptor, so it might not look like your
input).

``` r

pipe <- winpipe("sd-pipe", sddl = sd)
np_sd(pipe)
#> <winpipe_sd>
#> O:S-1-5-21-1492369709-893483088-3947136618-1001G:S-1-5-21-1492369709-893483088-3947136618-1001D:(D;;FA;;;WD)(A;;FA;;;BA)(A;;FA;;;SY)
```

## Related work

- [`processx`](https://processx.r-lib.org/) can emulate named pipes as
  child processes
- [`httppipe`](https://github.com/richfitz/httppipe) uses `reticulate`
  to communicate with named pipes through Python

# Package index

## All functions

- [`ace()`](https://jslth.github.io/winpipe/reference/ace.md) : Create
  an access control entry
- [`np_config()`](https://jslth.github.io/winpipe/reference/info.md)
  [`np_state()`](https://jslth.github.io/winpipe/reference/info.md)
  [`np_peek()`](https://jslth.github.io/winpipe/reference/info.md)
  [`np_connected()`](https://jslth.github.io/winpipe/reference/info.md)
  [`np_sd()`](https://jslth.github.io/winpipe/reference/info.md) :
  Low-level information about a named pipe
- [`np_whoami()`](https://jslth.github.io/winpipe/reference/np_whoami.md)
  [`np_token_info()`](https://jslth.github.io/winpipe/reference/np_whoami.md)
  : Security token information
- [`np_proxy()`](https://jslth.github.io/winpipe/reference/proxy.md)
  [`np_relay()`](https://jslth.github.io/winpipe/reference/proxy.md) :
  Proxies
- [`sd_create()`](https://jslth.github.io/winpipe/reference/security_descriptor.md)
  [`sd_add()`](https://jslth.github.io/winpipe/reference/security_descriptor.md)
  [`sd_build()`](https://jslth.github.io/winpipe/reference/security_descriptor.md)
  [`sd_parse()`](https://jslth.github.io/winpipe/reference/security_descriptor.md)
  [`sd_default()`](https://jslth.github.io/winpipe/reference/security_descriptor.md)
  : Build, parse and inspect security descriptors
- [`np_set_timeout()`](https://jslth.github.io/winpipe/reference/timeout.md)
  [`np_get_timeout()`](https://jslth.github.io/winpipe/reference/timeout.md)
  : Named pipe timeouts
- [`winpipe()`](https://jslth.github.io/winpipe/reference/winpipe.md)
  [`open(`*`<winpipe>`*`)`](https://jslth.github.io/winpipe/reference/winpipe.md)
  [`is_winpipe()`](https://jslth.github.io/winpipe/reference/winpipe.md)
  [`np_listen()`](https://jslth.github.io/winpipe/reference/winpipe.md)
  [`np_disconnect()`](https://jslth.github.io/winpipe/reference/winpipe.md)
  [`np_exists()`](https://jslth.github.io/winpipe/reference/winpipe.md)
  [`np_list()`](https://jslth.github.io/winpipe/reference/winpipe.md) :
  Named pipes
